title: Pluggable KV reservoir with opportunistic hole-mending allocator
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current KV cache allocator fragments under mixed-length workloads and sustained continuous-batching patterns. Fragmentation increases GPU memory pressure, causes uneven slot utilization across models, and forces fallback/unexpected evictions that degrade tail latency for production customers.

Proposal: Implement a pluggable 'reservoir' allocation layer that groups allocations into micro-reservoirs by allocation-size class and model/tenant affinity, combined with an opportunistic hole-mending strategy executed at allocation time and a low-priority background coalescer. Key ideas: 1) size-class reservoirs reduce small-object churn and avoid scattering many tiny free holes across the pool; 2) affinity-aware reservoirs reduce cross-model fragmentation for dedicated pools; 3) opportunistic hole-mending fixes adjacent free slots whenever we encounter candidate holes during an allocation path (cheap pointer updates instead of a full compaction pass); 4) coalescer is rate-limited and works during low-GPU utilization windows to perform larger defrag operations.

Design details:  - Allocation unit: carve the KV pool into slab pages (configurable: 128KB, 256KB) and further into size-classes (power-of-two micro-slots). Allocation requests map to nearest size-class and prefer free slots from the reservoir for that class.
  - Reservoirs: per-GPU and optional per-model reservoirs. Reservoir metadata is compact (bitmap + free-list) so we avoid large CPU-side overhead. Each reservoir maintains a soft-cap and a refill/evict policy based on recent allocation rate and LRU within the size-class.
  - Opportunistic hole-mending: when allocating into a page and seeing one or more small free holes adjacent to a candidate free run, the allocator will merge those holes into the run if the merging cost is <= threshold (few pointer ops and shadow-metadata updates). This reduces fragmentation without scheduling heavy compaction.
  - Background coalescer: a low-priority worker that scans pages with high hole density and attempts compaction by moving live KV entries into reclaimed contiguous regions. Movement honors model affinity; compaction is promiscuous for global pools and conservative for model-isolated pools. The coalescer uses pinned streams and waits for KV entries to be cold (no recent access) or checkpointed.
  - Integration with continuous batching: the allocator exposes an API for batch-aware prefetch of KV slots (reserve N contiguous slots for an in-flight batch) so that single-batch hot sequences avoid scatter and reduce per-token kernel overhead. We will align size-class boundaries with the 95th percentile KV key lengths observed in production traces so that typical batch KV growth stays within same reservoir.
  - Telemetry and knobs: metrics for fragmentation ratio (free holes bytes / total pool), median contiguous-run size, opportunistic-mends count, coalescer throughput, allocation latency p50/p99, and effective wasted memory. Config knobs: reservoir-size-by-class, mend-cost-threshold, coalescer-rate-limit, enable-per-model-reservoirs.

Migration path: ship the allocator behind a runtime feature flag. Start with per-GPU global reservoirs only (no per-model isolation) to validate memory/reliability impact. Flip on opportunistic mending via canary and monitor mem-pressure/latency for 72 hours before enabling background coalescer. For Dedicated customers with strict isolation, default to conservative per-model reservoirs and disable cross-model compaction unless enterprise opts in.

Backward compatibility: existing KV APIs remain unchanged. Existing KV entries are still addressable; compaction will use a remapping table that we persist to the checkpoint to avoid pointer invalidation. We will provide a migration utility that scans active pools and populates reservoirs without requiring full eviction (best-effort warm-up).

Alternatives considered: 1) Full stop-the-world compaction on threshold (rejected — too disruptive to tail latency). 2) Strict segregated pools by object age only (rejected — causes underutilization for bursty tenants). 3) Reference-counted moving GC for KV (rejected due to complexity and GPU synchronization costs).

Performance targets: reduce fragmentation overhead (wasted bytes) by >=40% on mixed-length traces, reduce OOM/retry incidents by >=30% during high-concurrency continuous-batching tests, keep allocation latency p99 under 2ms additional overhead for small allocations.

Open questions:  - Best default reservoir sizing heuristics across different GPU memory footprints?  - Mend threshold tuning for different GPU architectures (A100 vs H100) and NUMA topologies.  - Observability hooks needed to correlate request traces to defrag activity for postmortems.

acceptance_criteria: 1) Feature flag gates allocator and can be toggled per-deploy; 2) Canary run shows fragmentation ratio reduction >=25% within 72h with no increase in p99 tail latency beyond 5%; 3) No regressed OOMs or correctness issues in checkpoint/restore; 4) Telemetry surfaces opportunistic-mend and coalescer metrics in Console; 5) Documented runbook for forced compaction and rollback.
